workflow.title: Klinswork Project Change and Documentation Workflow
workflow.purpose: Define the complete controlled cycle for selecting a project milestone, preserving the pre-work understanding in a structured intention record, planning and performing the work in a bounded session, testing the intended result, documenting what actually occurred, reconciling project and integration state, evaluating the planning template, generating publication artifacts, updating indexes, and closing the run.
revisionSummary: Moved the workflow start from the work session to a pre-work project review.
Added a preserved work-session intention record with explicit definition of done, anticipated integrations, and planned acceptance tests.
Separated the durable project roadmap from the session-specific implementation plan.
Defined a fresh ChatGPT conversation as a bounded execution environment with a registered context package.
Added plan amendments that preserve rather than rewrite the original intention baseline.
Added planned tests, real-use verification, and evidence collection before the documentation checkpoint.
Moved project and integration reconciliation into the post-work analysis and debrief cycle.
Added evaluation of the work-session-intention template for effectiveness and efficiency after project records are updated.
Added integration IDs, lifecycle references, authority rules, and integration coverage declarations.
Changed the sidecar target from the v2 draft to a future project-aware v3 draft.
Retained publication, catalog, image, Google Sites, communication, and final verification stages.
Added a stopping rule so routine documentation production does not recursively trigger another full documentation run.

durable project purpose, boundaries, principles, and historical explanation
planned project direction, milestones, priorities, deferred work, and next steps
current integration identity, direction, ownership, authority, lifecycle state, and verification status
the understanding, intended intervention, expected effects, and acceptance criteria that existed before work began
the tactical sequence chosen to perform one bounded session of work
what actually happened during the body of work, including evidence, reasoning, comparison with intention, and proposed change interpretation
the result of comparing intention, implementation, evidence, and updated project truth

designPrinciples: Current project and integration context must be loaded before a work intention is approved.
The original work-session intention is a preserved baseline and must not be rewritten to agree with later results.
Changes to intention or scope during execution are recorded as timestamped amendments.
The durable project roadmap and the session-specific implementation plan are separate artifacts.
Definition of done and acceptance tests are designed before implementation whenever possible.
Anticipated project and integration effects are hypotheses until confirmed by work evidence.
A fresh work-session conversation should receive a bounded context package rather than the entire documentation repository.
Stable project, product, integration, document, milestone, decision, and session IDs are used instead of names as identifiers.
Projects are nodes, integrations are durable edges, and work updates record changes to nodes and edges.
Each data domain has one authoritative owner even when other projects display or reference its records.
Integration omission is meaningful only when the declared coverage requires complete integration reporting.
Current truth, historical truth, and planned truth remain distinguishable.
The work narrative must preserve chronology, causation, wrong turns, amendments, and turning points.
Project and integration state are reconciled after work evidence has been interpreted and before publication artifacts are finalized.
The intention template is evaluated after project and integration records have been updated.
Template revisions are versioned and supported by session evaluations rather than silently replacing prior versions.
The approved summary is the authoritative narrative source for downstream publication artifacts.
Individual sidecars are retained after catalog aggregation.
Canonical URLs are distinguished from temporary, historical, replaced, or unresolved URLs.
Generated catalogs, metadata, indexes, and manifests are validated against their source records.
Focused instruction sets are loaded at workflow boundaries rather than keeping all procedures continuously in context.
Missing records are acknowledged rather than invented.
Ordinary use of the documentation workflow does not itself require a new full documentation run unless the workflow, schema, authority rules, or capabilities changed materially.

workflowStates.description: A potential milestone or change has been identified but project context and scope have not yet been established.
The primary project, related projects, integrations, current state, roadmap, and authoritative records have been loaded.
The work-session intention record is being drafted and reviewed.
The pre-work intention, definition of done, anticipated effects, and acceptance tests have been approved and frozen as a baseline.
A bounded execution conversation and context package have been created and recorded.
The tactical implementation strategy, checkpoints, tests, and recovery considerations have been reviewed.
Active building, testing, troubleshooting, discussion, and decision-making are underway.
The intended stopping point has been reached or explicitly classified, and planned or necessary tests have produced evidence.
Active work has paused and the bounded body of work is ready for interpretation and preservation.
The actual work, evidence, intention comparison, and proposed project and integration changes are being reconstructed.
The evidence-supported interpretation of what changed has been approved for reconciliation.
Project files, roadmaps, and integration records have been updated while preserving prior state and provenance.
The session has been compared against its intention and implementation plan, and the planning template has been evaluated.
The final authoritative summary reflects the reconciled project state and completed debrief.
The public HTML and individual sidecar have been created from the approved summary and current authoritative records.
The summary, HTML, sidecar, IDs, anchors, integration references, and publication fields have passed validation.
The sidecar has been aggregated and catalog metadata regenerated.
The work-update image has been generated, saved, and added to the image manifest.
Artifacts have been committed, pushed, indexed, and made available through canonical URLs and selected portal references.
Communication disposition, final verification, exceptions, and template-learning outputs have been recorded and the cycle is closed.

globalInputTypes: recent summaries, sidecars, decisions, and work updates
current conversation and planned work discussion
screenshots, tests, logs, and console output
globalOutputTypes: documentation index and Google Sites entry

instructionSets.purpose: Create the run record, select the target milestone, and load the minimum authoritative context.
Guide creation of the preserved pre-work intention, effects forecast, scope, and definition of done.
Turn the approved intention into a tactical implementation and test strategy.
Guide evidence collection, amendments, testing, and milestone classification during execution.
Switch from performing work to interpreting and preserving it.
Guide creation of the intention-aware, project-aware narrative source summary.
Reconcile the approved change interpretation against project, roadmap, and integration authorities.
Compare intention with result and evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the planning template.
Generate the public HTML and supervisor reading path from the final approved summary.
Describe the finished HTML with authoritative project IDs, integration IDs, coverage, publication fields, and provenance.
Generate the visual artifact from approved publication material.
Publish artifacts, record canonical URLs, rebuild the documentation index, and prepare portal references.
Record communication disposition, verify all outputs, and close the cycle.

phases.title: Establish the Current Project and Integration Context
Define and Freeze the Work-Session Intention
Register and Plan the Work Session
Perform, Amend, and Verify the Work
Generate and Validate the Document Artifacts
Create and Index the Visual Artifact
Publish and Update the Documentation Portals
Communicate, Verify, and Close the Run

steps.title: Create the run record and select the project-change target
steps.purpose: Establish a durable identity for the cycle and identify the milestone or problem being considered.
inputs: candidate roadmap items or operational needs
actions: select a provisional primary project and milestone candidate
record why the change is being considered
validation: The run and session IDs are unique.
The candidate change is described without claiming implementation.
Missing authorities are recorded explicitly.

steps.title: Load authoritative project, roadmap, and integration context
steps.purpose: Establish the current truth from which the intended intervention will begin.
inputs: product and data records when relevant
actions: load related projects only when materially relevant
load current roadmap and milestone status
load active, planned, degraded, deprecated, and superseded integrations
identify data authorities and downstream consumers
validation: Current state is distinguished from plans and historical records.
Integration IDs and authority claims resolve where records exist.
Stale or missing context is labeled.

steps.title: Confirm the milestone boundary and related entities
steps.purpose: Define the likely project, product, data, integration, and documentation boundaries before drafting intention.
inputs: affected applications, datasets, and operational processes
actions: identify related projects and shared foundations
distinguish project changes from application-version changes
validation: Projects are not inferred merely because they are mentioned.
Apps, releases, components, datasets, and projects are distinguished.
The proposed scope is narrow enough for one intentional work session or milestone.

steps.title: Load the work-session intention template
steps.purpose: Load the questions and rules used to preserve the pre-work understanding.
actions: load required identity, purpose, scope, effect, risk, test, and context-package fields
validation: The template version is recorded.
The template distinguishes facts, assumptions, expectations, and unknowns.
The template requires a definition of done or an explicit exception.

steps.title: Draft work-session-intention.json
steps.purpose: Preserve what is intended, expected, and considered relevant before implementation changes the understanding.
actions: state the prompting problem or opportunity
state the intended change and expected result
identify anticipated project and integration effects
identify data authorities and expected record propagation
define acceptance, regression, and real-use tests
identify risks, assumptions, rollback considerations, and required context
validation: Expected effects are labeled as hypotheses.
Integration IDs are used when available.
The definition of done is observable.
Tests are capable of distinguishing success from partial or failed results.

steps.title: Review, approve, and freeze the intention baseline
steps.purpose: Create an immutable pre-work baseline for later comparison.
actions: review factual and project placement accuracy
confirm acceptance tests and operational examples
prohibit in-place rewriting after execution begins
outputs: frozen baseline checksum or version identifier
validation: The user approves the intention.
The baseline is preserved for later comparison.
Future changes must be recorded as amendments.

steps.title: Open and register the bounded work-session conversation
steps.purpose: Start execution in a fresh conversation with deliberate provenance and bounded context.
actions: open a new conversation in the Documentation project or other designated execution space
provide the intention and bounded context package
verify the context package is readable
link the conversation, intention, session, and run IDs
validation: The new conversation can identify its project, session, intention, and target milestone.
Only materially relevant context is loaded.
The run record contains the execution conversation reference.

steps.title: Inspect the implementation and create the session plan
steps.purpose: Translate the intended result into a tactical implementation strategy after inspecting the actual system.
inputs: relevant source files and current implementation
actions: identify likely files, services, sheets, records, and interfaces
identify discrepancies between assumed and actual implementation
validation: The plan is distinct from ROADMAP.md.
The plan addresses the approved definition of done.
Any contradiction with the intention is surfaced rather than silently changed.

steps.title: Review and approve the implementation and test strategy
steps.purpose: Confirm that the tactical plan is feasible, bounded, and capable of producing interpretable evidence.
actions: approve necessary pre-work amendments without rewriting the baseline
validation: The plan can be traced to intention fields and acceptance criteria.
Known integration risks have a test or explicit disposition.
The user approves execution.

steps.title: Perform the work
steps.purpose: Build, modify, configure, migrate, or otherwise carry out the bounded project change.
actions: collect screenshots, logs, outputs, changed files, and deployment evidence
preserve the actual chronology and causation
validation: Changes remain within scope or trigger an amendment.
Evidence is collected as work proceeds.
Unverified behavior is not presented as complete.

steps.title: Append intention and plan amendments
steps.purpose: Preserve how understanding, scope, dependencies, and strategy changed during execution.
actions: record why each change became necessary
classify scope as unchanged, narrowed, expanded, redirected, or superseded
record newly discovered projects, integrations, data propagation, risks, and tests
validation: The original baseline remains unchanged.
Each material scope change has a reason and consequence.
Newly discovered integration effects are not retroactively labeled as anticipated.

steps.title: Run acceptance, regression, and real-use verification
steps.purpose: Determine whether the intended result was achieved and capture evidence across affected project and integration boundaries.
actions: perform realistic end-to-end or real-use tests where appropriate
inspect downstream records and integration effects
record additional tests required by discoveries
classify each test as passed, failed, partial, blocked, deferred, or not applicable
validation: Every completion condition has a result or explicit disposition.
Actual data and integration effects are checked where the intention predicted them.
Test failures and deferred tests are preserved.

steps.title: Declare the final milestone and documentation checkpoint
steps.purpose: Bound the body of work and determine whether it is complete, partial, superseded, abandoned, or ready for another implementation cycle.
actions: identify where the documented work begins and ends
identify unfinished work outside the documentation boundary
record whether another work loop is required before documentation
validation: The boundary is clear enough to summarize.
The result is compared with the original definition of done.
Incomplete work is not falsely presented as complete.

steps.title: Load documentation-checkpoint and summary instructions
steps.purpose: Switch from execution to evidence-based interpretation.
actions: load required summary sections and quality checks
load project and integration change mappings
validation: The instructions identify current inputs, expected outputs, and next stage.
The summary is required to distinguish anticipated, discovered, confirmed, and unobserved effects.

steps.title: Construct the draft summary and proposed project/integration delta
steps.purpose: Create the narrative and analytical account of what actually occurred, using the intention as a preserved before-state.
actions: write project context and situation before work
preserve chronology, decisions, wrong turns, amendments, and turning points
classify planned tests and additional tests
describe actual project and integration effects
draft integration lifecycle and verification changes
validation: The summary does not rewrite the intention baseline.
Actual effects are distinguished from forecasts.
Completed, partial, failed, deferred, and newly discovered work are classified.
The proposed deltas are traceable to evidence.

steps.title: Review evidence and approve the change interpretation
steps.purpose: Confirm the evidence-supported account that will be used to update current project and integration truth.
actions: restore missing causation and turning points
approve the project and integration change interpretation
validation: Every current-state change has evidence or an explicit human decision.
Integration IDs and authority changes are valid.
The user approves reconciliation.

steps.title: Derive the final project, roadmap, and integration delta
steps.purpose: Translate the approved interpretation into explicit updates while preserving prior state.
actions: classify prior work as completed, partial, still open, deferred, superseded, or invalidated
classify integration changes as planned, implemented, changed, verified, degraded, deprecated, superseded, retired, or unchanged
validation: No prior roadmap item disappears without classification.
Integration status changes retain introduced, changed, verified, superseded, and retired provenance.
New inference is labeled.

steps.title: Update project files, roadmap, and integration authorities
steps.purpose: Make the new current truth authoritative while preserving historical truth and plans.
actions: update current project state and products
update integration lifecycle, authority, direction, and verification fields
preserve completed, deferred, superseded, and prior-state history
link intention, session, summary, tests, and future publication records
validation: Earlier state is not silently overwritten.
Current truth agrees with approved evidence.
Project and integration records use stable IDs.
The revised roadmap agrees with the work result.

steps.title: Debrief the session and evaluate the intention template
steps.purpose: Compare the original intention, implementation strategy, evidence, and updated project truth; then evaluate how well the planning instrument performed.
actions: classify intended-and-achieved, intended-not-achieved, achieved-differently, unexpectedly-achieved, disproved, and deferred outcomes
compare anticipated and actual project/integration effects
identify questions not asked but needed
evaluate preparation time, context sufficiency, amendment burden, and avoided reconstruction
validation: Evaluation occurs after current project truth has been updated.
The original intention instance is not modified.
Effectiveness and efficiency are evaluated separately.
Recommendations cite evidence from the session.

steps.title: Finalize and approve the authoritative summary
steps.purpose: Incorporate reconciled current state and debrief results into the narrative source used by publication artifacts.
actions: update resulting state and roadmap sections
record actual integration changes and current authority
record template-learning outcomes when materially relevant
validation: The summary agrees with current project and integration authorities.
The summary preserves the historical before-state.
All applicable quality checks pass.
The user approves the summary as the downstream narrative source.

steps.title: Generate the work-update HTML
steps.purpose: Create the full public narrative and the alternate supervisor reading path.
actions: generate the complete narrative and technical document
add a gold Supervisor Brief near the beginning
add links to the next supervisor note
add stable anchors and accessible labels
validation: The HTML is valid and readable.
Supervisor callouts are distinct and ordered.
The full account remains available outside the skim path.

steps.title: Generate and retain the individual v3 sidecar
steps.purpose: Describe the finished HTML using authoritative project, product, integration, publication, and provenance records.
actions: record authoritative primary and related project IDs
record integration references and changes by stable ID
record narrative structure and project contribution
record technical evidence, communications, graphics, publication, deployment, and provenance
validation: The sidecar is valid JSON.
The sidecar accurately describes the finished HTML.
Project and integration descriptions agree with current authorities while preserving historical labels.
The sidecar does not replace project, integration, intention, or workflow-run records.

steps.title: Validate summary, HTML, sidecar, IDs, and coverage
steps.purpose: Catch structural, authority, lifecycle, coverage, linkage, and publication errors before indexing.
actions: check HTML anchors and supervisor navigation
validate sidecar schema and document ID uniqueness
resolve every project, product, integration, document, and session ID
check integration lifecycle and authority consistency
check integration-coverage declaration and omission semantics
check alt text, listing title, listing description, canonical URL handling, and provenance
validation: All blocking validation errors are resolved.
Narrative and project interpretation have human review.
A narrow sidecar is not falsely validated as a complete project or system snapshot.

steps.title: Append the validated sidecar to the cumulative catalog
steps.purpose: Add the new document record to the searchable aggregate without losing the individual source record.
actions: retain historical names and versions while using canonical project IDs
validation: The sidecar appears exactly once.
No unrelated record is altered.
The individual sidecar remains available.
Canonical project IDs do not erase historical document terminology.

steps.title: Regenerate catalog metadata and validate the catalog
steps.purpose: Recalculate catalog summaries and verify aggregate consistency using canonical identities.
actions: recalculate entry count and date range
recalculate canonical projects, products, applications, topics, integrations, document types, and versions
rebuild document ID and title lists
validation: Entry counts agree.
Every expected sidecar appears exactly once.
Canonical and historical names are not conflated.
Metadata and catalog fields are internally consistent.

steps.title: Generate the work-update image
steps.purpose: Create a visual artifact representing the significance of the documented work.
actions: select relevant applications, records, or relationships
validation: The image represents the documented significance rather than an incidental screenshot.
The image has appropriate alt text.
The image follows the intended publication format.

steps.title: Save and index the image
steps.purpose: Store the image and update the image manifest with project and document relationships.
actions: record document, project, product, and integration relationships when relevant
validation: The image file exists at the expected path.
The manifest contains it exactly once.
Description, alt text, and document relationship are present.

steps.title: Commit, push, and record canonical URLs
steps.purpose: Publish the coordinated records and establish canonical resource locations.
inputs: intention and run records when published
actions: record GitHub Pages document and image URLs
record canonical Apps Script /exec URLs when applicable
update sidecar, catalog, and metadata when post-publication URLs become available
validation: Public resources are accessible where expected.
Temporary runtime URLs are not canonical.
Post-publication structured records are regenerated when URLs change.

steps.title: Regenerate the documentation index and update selected portal references
steps.purpose: Expose the new document through the canonical generated index and, when selected, the curated Google Sites portal.
actions: regenerate and publish the canonical documentation index
verify the new work update appears
read listingTitle and listingDescription from the sidecar
update Google Sites manually when selected
point the Google Sites reference to the canonical GitHub Pages document
outputs: Google Sites entry or intentional omission record
validation: Project, date, topic, integration, and document links resolve correctly.
Google Sites text comes from structured publication fields rather than improvisation.
Portal omission is recorded when intentional.

steps.title: Communicate, verify all outputs, and close the run
steps.purpose: Record communication disposition, verify the complete cycle, and preserve final status and learning outputs.
actions: send the update or record intentional omission
verify intention, implementation plan, evidence, project updates, integration updates, debrief, evaluation, summary, HTML, sidecar, catalog, metadata, image, manifest, URLs, index, and portal status
record whether template changes are recommendations or promoted revisions
validation: All required artifacts exist or missing artifacts are explicitly recorded.
Communication is sent or intentionally omitted.
The run has a clear final status.
Routine workflow execution does not recursively create another run unless the documentation system changed materially.

blockingConditions: No stable primary project ID has been selected when project records are available.
The work-session intention has not been approved and frozen before execution begins.
Definition of done or acceptance criteria are absent without an explicit documented exception.
The execution conversation cannot be linked to the intention record and run record.
An amendment overwrites the original intention instead of preserving the baseline.
The milestone disposition or test evidence is missing at the documentation checkpoint.
The change interpretation has not been approved before current project or integration state is updated.
A prior roadmap item disappears without classification.
A referenced project, product, integration, document, or session ID does not exist.
An integration authority claim conflicts with the authoritative integration record.
A complete-project or complete-system integration snapshot omits an active required integration without explanation.
The final summary has not been approved after project reconciliation and debrief.
The work-update HTML is missing or structurally invalid.
The sidecar JSON is invalid or does not match the finished HTML.
A sidecar uses an integration marked retired or superseded without historical qualification.
The document ID is missing or duplicated.
Supervisor navigation contains broken anchors.
Catalog and metadata counts disagree.
The image manifest references a missing image.
A temporary Apps Script URL is presented as canonical.
Publication claims cannot be verified.
nonBlockingConditions: A bootstrap or legacy project record remains provisional and is clearly labeled.
An anticipated integration effect was not observed.
A planned acceptance test was intentionally deferred and the reason is recorded.
A session-level template recommendation has not yet been promoted into a reusable template revision.
Google Sites has not been manually updated for an update not selected for portal publication.
Supervisor communication has been intentionally omitted.
A knowledge-base candidate has not yet been promoted.
A canonical URL is unavailable before publication.
A legacy sidecar has not yet been migrated to the current schema.

resolvedDesignDecisions.decision: The controlled cycle begins before implementation with project review and an intention record.
The approved intention record is preserved; later scope changes are append-only amendments.
ROADMAP.md represents durable project direction; implementation-plan.md represents one session's tactical strategy.
A fresh bounded ChatGPT work conversation is registered and started from a prepared context package.
Projects are nodes, integrations have stable IDs as edges, and work updates record changes to those edges.
Project and integration records are updated before the intention template is evaluated; final publication artifacts are generated afterward.
Each run may produce template recommendations; reusable template revisions are versioned and supported by evaluation evidence.
Routine documentation execution does not trigger a separate full run unless the documentation system itself changed materially.

What exact fields and required questions will version 1 of work-session-intention-template.json contain?
Should implementation plans remain Markdown, use JSON, or use a Markdown document with structured front matter?
Should debrief.json remain separate or become a section of documentation-run.json?
Which template defects justify immediate revision and which require a recurring pattern across several evaluations?
How will project authorities, integration references, integration changes, and coverage declarations be represented in sidecar v3?
Where will the generated canonical documentation index be hosted?
currentCandidates: Apps Script if private or Workspace-integrated behavior becomes necessary
